historical_proof_status.summary: Problem 30, printed p.19: restricted regular two-group components: Canonical bounded cores classify ordered nondegenerate regular two-group markings at fixed excess. A global marked-kernel basis gives every class-at-most-three marking in every rank, with a two-state transfer formula and Fibonacci total. Separated first-excess cores give the unrestricted leading coefficient 5^k/k! and a lower-degree higher-class contribution.; Companion complete excess-two ordered-marking classification: For d>=3, exactly (25d^2-107d+122)/2 nondegenerate ordered string C-group markings of order 2^(2d+1). Of these 9d-20 have class four: 4d-8 with cyclic gamma3, and 5d-12 with elementary-abelian gamma3. The exact constructions and marked presentations establish completeness. Lean verifies the nested-kernel IP adapter under its explicit profile assumptions, not the full classification. The independent rank-three quotient census is a bounded diagnostic. No additional principal-paper credit or priority claim.; Companion finite-state classification at every fixed nilpotency class: For fixed c>=2, ordered nondegenerate finite two-group string C-groups of class at most c correspond exactly to accepted walks in an effectively finite graph of c-windows and boundary deletion kernels. Compatible semidirect/diagonal gluing, coset Helly and exact deletion update prove construction, actual IP and uniqueness. The rank/excess generating function is rational. At excess k>=1, class<=k+2 and windows of order<=2^(3k+3) suffice. No efficient general library enumeration, unmarked/chiral classification or full Problem30 resolution is claimed.; Companion exact third-excess ordered-marking count in every rank: For rank d>=4 and order2^(2d+2), a3(d)=(125d^3-855d^2+2380d-2646)/6; rank3 has37. All706 rank-five windows give708 states and1522 edges. The exact2832-coordinate identity (T-I)^4 v7=0 gives an alternate all-rank proof without the eventual-polynomiality input. Ranks4–6 use separate exact bases. GAP/NQ and the finite-state completeness theorem remain inputs; no unmarked or reversal count, whole-problem solution or priority claim.

Exact unrestricted excess-three counts are now supplied by a complete finite graph and integer-vector certificate; higher excess coefficients remain uncomputed. This is progress on a restricted component, not a solution of Problem 30 or a rederivation of the survey. Publication priority, complete formalization and a matched proof-length ratio remain unestablished.
